_comment: Explicit exceptions to the local clock-gating rules (tools/check-cg.py, docs/rtl-coding-style.md 'Local clock gating'). One entry per module, rule (CG-1, CG-2 or CG-3) and register; why says what was measured and why the rule cannot or should not be met. A waiver that excuses nothing is refused.

waivers.why: A repeater stage exists because its input arrives after a cycle of wire. Any enable that could tell a new valid from a held one has to see that input, and an ICG enable must set up before the flop's own D does, so it would turn a wire-limited path into a gate-limited one. The pulse flops are 3 * SLOTS + 1 a stage; the payload, which is most of the flops, is gated by this flop (CG-2 0.0 NGD, DCGE 79-100%).
As valid_q: the credit arrives over the link's wire, so an enable that sees it reaches the clock gate late.
As valid_q: the stall arrives over the link's wire, so an enable that sees it reaches the clock gate late.
As valid_q: the wake arrives over the link's wire, so an enable that sees it reaches the clock gate late. One flop a stage.

The registered wake is the one path from another block into the gate, and Q-49 ends it at a flop so it never reaches a clock gate's enable. An enable that saw `wake` would put it back there. One flop.

8.9 NGD measured, against 7.4 for q_run_q, whose enable is the same logic: a 6-bit compare against the hysteresis CSR beside a zero test, then a mux. The compare is on the path because a threshold lowered mid-count takes effect at once (docs/clock-gate.md); registering it would take a CSR change one cycle late, which changes the proved hysteresis. DCGE is 100% in every scenario. Raised for Daniel with the clock-gating rule.
